findings.title: State-of-the-art claim supported by a single baseline
findings.quote: Table 1 compares HybridNet with a support vector machine baseline.
findings.why_it_matters: Beating one SVM does not show superiority over existing approaches; strong tabular methods such as gradient-boosted trees or random forests are standard on this dataset.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare against a simple baseline (logistic regression) and strong tabular models (random forest, gradient boosting) under the same split, preprocessing and tuning budget, or narrow the claim.

findings.title: No ablation study for the three-component architecture
findings.quote: HybridNet consists of three components: a 1-D convolutional block with 64 filters, an LSTM module with 32 units, and an attention mechanism, followed by a dense output layer.
findings.why_it_matters: It is unknown whether the CNN, the LSTM or the attention mechanism is responsible for the result, or whether a simpler model would do as well.
findings.suggested_fix: Report results with each component removed or replaced under the same protocol.

findings.title: Tuning effort for the SVM baseline not described
findings.quote: Table 1 compares HybridNet with a support vector machine baseline.
findings.why_it_matters: If HybridNet was tuned and the SVM was not, the comparison favours HybridNet.
findings.suggested_fix: State the SVM kernel and hyperparameter search and give it the same tuning budget.
